outcome: Since 26 January 2024 no mathematical progress on Goodman's coefficient inequality for p-valent functions was found: the only window events are a 2026 Lean formal statement of the inequality (issue #3477 opened 8 March 2026; PR #4435 merged 13 September 2026) with the conjecture itself left as sorry, and no paper, announcement or AI claim of a proof, counterexample or new bound turned up.
problem_asks: The bullet names one conjecture and states no inequality: 'Goodman's conjecture on the coefficients of multivalent functions'. The content the name points to, as the linked article and the formal entry both state it, has these parts. (1) For every integer p >= 1 and every p-valent function f on the unit disk, written as a power series f(z) = sum of b_n z^n. (2) For every n beyond p (the formal statement takes n > p; the article gives no range), |b_n| is at most a weighted sum over k = 1..p of |b_k|, with weights 2k(n+p)! / ((p-k)! (p+k)! (n-p-1)! (n^2 - k^2)). Read as separate asks: the inequality for general p (not only p = 2 or 3, and not only special classes); for every n beyond p; bounded by the weighted sum over the first p coefficients. The p = 1 instance reduces to |b_n| <= n|b_1|, which for b_1 = 1 is the Bieberbach bound proved by de Branges in 1985, so it is covered as a special case. The bullet does not ask for sharpness or equality cases. The inequality itself is taken from the linked article, because the bullet does not state it.

events.what_happened: A. W. Goodman states the p-valent coefficient conjecture in his Columbia dissertation and in 'On some determinants related to p-valent functions', Trans. AMS 63 (1948) 175-192. This is the origin of the conjecture, not a result on it. I did not open the paper (the AMS page was not retrievable); its existence and title come from the Wikipedia article's references and a search snippet.
events.delivers: Nothing on the problem's status: it introduces the conjecture. Wikipedia's infobox dates the thesis to 1947 while its text dates the conjecture to 1948, so the first written version is dated to 1947 or 1948.
events.direction: Poses the conjecture; no direction of result.

events.what_happened: A. W. Goodman and M. S. Robertson, 'A class of multivalent functions', Trans. AMS 70 (1951) 127-136 (MR 40430). A search summary of the paper's introduction says the authors prove the inequality for a class T(p) of p-valent functions defined in their section 2. A later search summary attributes to a later Robertson paper (not located) the statement that the result settles the problem for real coefficients and arbitrary p. I could not open the paper: the AMS page returned 403.
events.delivers: Per the first secondary summary only: the Goodman inequality for functions in a restricted class T(p). Per the second: the inequality for real coefficients and arbitrary p. The two descriptions conflict in scope and I could not resolve them from the paper.
events.remains: Per the first description: the inequality for p-valent functions outside T(p), that is the general conjecture. Per the second: complex coefficients.

checked_by.who: Transactions of the American Mathematical Society (refereed journal)

events.doubts: The two secondary descriptions disagree on scope (restricted class T(p) against real coefficients for arbitrary p). Neither was read from the paper, and journal acceptance does not establish which scope is right.
events.direction: Proves the conjectured inequality, in the conjectured direction, for at least a restricted class.

events.what_happened: A. E. Livingston, 'The coefficients of multivalent close-to-convex functions', Proc. AMS 21 (1969) 545-552. A search summary drawing on a 2018 Sharma note says the paper proves Goodman's inequality for p-valent close-to-convex functions when a_1 = ... = a_(p-2) = 0 and the remaining coefficients may be complex. I did not open the paper.
events.delivers: Per the summary only: the inequality for p-valent close-to-convex functions under the vanishing condition a_1 ... a_(p-2) = 0, with complex coefficients allowed. Nothing for other p-valent classes.
events.remains: All p-valent functions outside the close-to-convex class, and all without the vanishing condition.
events.doubts: Known only through a secondary summary; the exact vanishing condition comes from that summary.
events.direction: Proves the conjectured inequality, in the conjectured direction, for a restricted class and restricted coefficients.

events.what_happened: R. Miniowitz, 'On almost bounded functions', Trans. AMS 223 (1976) 93-102. The abstract, as quoted in a search result (I did not open the page), says one theorem proves 'Goodman's conjecture in a particular case'. A search summary ties the paper to Goodman's own 1955 work on almost bounded functions, so the conjecture meant may be a different Goodman conjecture.
events.delivers: Unknown. If it is the p-valent conjecture, it proves one unspecified special case. The paper's text was not read.
events.doubts: It is not established that the 'Goodman conjecture' in this abstract is the p-valent coefficient conjecture; the summary points to a different object (almost bounded functions).

events.what_happened: A. Lyzzaik and D. Styer, 'Goodman's conjecture and the coefficients of univalent functions', Proc. AMS 69 (1978) 111-114, DOI 10.1090/S0002-9939-1978-0460619-7. Listed in the Wikipedia article's references. Grinshpan (1997) says his proof rests on a determinant theorem of Lyzzaik and Styer. The AMS pages returned 403, so I did not read the paper. One search summary reports that it shows Goodman's conjecture, for polynomial compositions, is equivalent to coefficient conjectures for normalized univalent functions; I could not verify this.
events.delivers: Not established from anything I read. Per Grinshpan, a determinant theorem used for the polynomial-composition reduction. The equivalence description is unverified.
events.doubts: Its content was not read. The equivalence description rests on a search summary.

events.what_happened: R. J. Leach, 'Coefficient estimates for certain multivalent functions', Pacific J. Math. 74 (1978) 133-142. The abstract, opened on msp.org, begins 'We prove the Goodman conjecture for a class of multivalent functions including close-to-convex functions.' It adds that the proof applies under the restriction that the coefficients are real, and that similar results hold for other classes. The full text was not read.
events.delivers: The Goodman inequality for a class of p-valent functions that includes the close-to-convex ones, under the restriction that the coefficients are real. Similar results for other classes, not specified in the abstract.
events.remains: Complex coefficients for the same class; p-valent functions outside the class; the full conjecture.
events.doubts: The abstract does not define the class; the exact class and the inequality were not read.
events.direction: Proves the conjectured inequality for a restricted class and restricted coefficients, in the conjectured direction.

events.what_happened: A. Z. Grinshpan, 'On an identity related to multivalent functions', Proc. AMS 123(4) (1995) 1199. Cited in the Wikipedia article's references. A search summary says it treats an algebraic identity used in the p-valent coefficient problem and cites the 1951 Goodman-Robertson paper. Not read.
events.delivers: Not established: the content was not read.

events.what_happened: P. G. Todorov, 'On the coefficients of p-valent functions which are polynomials of univalent functions', Proc. AMS 97 (1986) 605-608. The abstract, seen in a search result (the AMS page returned 403, so not opened): explicit formulas for coefficients of p-valent functions that are polynomials of univalent functions in the class S; these formulas settle the Goodman conjecture for f(z) = [phi(z)]^p with phi in S; sharp bounds in terms of the components.
events.delivers: Goodman's inequality for the special family f = phi^p with phi univalent, the p-th power of a univalent function. Only that family is covered by the abstract; sharp bounds are also given for the wider polynomial-of-univalent family.
events.remains: All p-valent functions outside the p-th-power family, and for general p the whole conjecture.
events.doubts: Known only from the abstract as it appeared in a search result. The proof was not read.
events.direction: Proves the conjectured inequality, in the conjectured direction, for a restricted family.

events.what_happened: A. Z. Grinshpan, 'On the Goodman conjecture and related functions of several complex variables', Algebra i Analiz 9(3) (1997) 198-204; English translation St. Petersburg Math. J. 9 (1998) 595-600 (per a search summary). The abstract, opened on geodesic.mathdoc.fr: the principal coefficient problem for p-valent functions (the Goodman conjecture) is considered for polynomial compositions; it is reduced to a coefficient conjecture for several complex variables related to univalent functions; the proof rests on the Lyzzaik-Styer determinant theorem; the paper also discusses advantages of the equivalent conjecture.
events.delivers: For polynomial compositions, the Goodman problem is reduced to an equivalent coefficient conjecture in several complex variables. The abstract describes a reduction and does not say the reduced conjecture is proved.
events.remains: The several-variables conjecture (not proved per the abstract); every p-valent function that is not a polynomial composition; the general conjecture.

checked_by.who: Algebra i Analiz (refereed journal); English translation in St. Petersburg Math. J. (refereed)

events.doubts: Wikipedia says the conjecture is known to hold for p = 2, 3 when f = P composed with phi, with P a polynomial and phi univalent. This 1997 abstract describes a reduction for that setting, not a proof. The Wikipedia text I read does not name the source of that statement.
events.direction: A reduction; by the abstract's wording it neither proves nor disproves the conjecture.

events.what_happened: S. Sahoo and N. L. Sharma, 'A note on a class of p-valent starlike functions of order beta', arXiv:1407.1196 (the month is inferred from the arXiv identifier), published in Siberian Math. J. 57(2) (2016). Gives sharp coefficient bounds for p-valent starlike functions of order beta and points out that an earlier proof by Aouf is incorrect. Discarded: a different class and inequality. The PDF was unreadable to me; the description comes from a search summary.
events.delivers: Coefficient bounds for p-valent starlike functions of order beta. Not the Goodman inequality as far as I could read.
events.remains: Nothing for Goodman's inequality is established by this paper.
events.direction: Not about the conjectured inequality; a different class.

events.what_happened: N. L. Sharma, 'A note on the coefficient estimates for some classes of p-valent functions', Ukrainian Math. J. 70(4) (2018), published 25 April 2018 per the journal page. The abstract, read on the landing page, says it estimates Taylor-Maclaurin coefficients of some classes of p-valent functions, revisits a problem of Aouf (1988), and says Aouf's proof was partly erroneous. The landing-page abstract does not mention Goodman's conjecture. A search summary says the body records Goodman's n = p+1 inequality for p-valent starlike and convex classes under vanishing and real-coefficient conditions; I did not verify this.
events.delivers: Estimates for certain p-valent classes, per its abstract. For Goodman's conjecture, nothing is established from the abstract; the body may restate Goodman's earlier special cases (unverified).
events.remains: All of problem_asks, as far as the abstract shows.
events.doubts: The Goodman special-case description comes from a search summary, not from the text. No earlier version was checked, so 25 April 2018 is the journal publication date.
events.direction: Different classes per its abstract; the Goodman special cases, if restated, are not new.

events.what_happened: F. G. Avkhadiev and K.-J. Wirths, 'Starlike cases of the generalized Goodman conjecture', 2013, per a search summary. No URL was retrieved and I did not open it. It concerns meromorphic univalent functions in the unit disk with a simple pole at a point of (0,1), and proves the generalized statement for two classes whose complement is starlike.
events.delivers: Not the p-valent inequality: a generalization to meromorphic univalent functions with a pole. Discarded for that reason.
events.remains: All of problem_asks, for the p-valent case.
events.doubts: Known only from a search summary; the venue and the exact statement are not confirmed.
events.direction: Different question: meromorphic univalent functions, not p-valent.

events.what_happened: GitHub issue google-deepmind/formal-conjectures #3477, 'Goodman's conjecture on coefficients of p-valent functions', opened 8 March 2026 by GitHub user franzhusch. It asks for the conjecture to be formalised (labels ams-30, ams-32, 'new conjecture', 'wikipedia'; milestone 'Wikipedia, Analysis'). The body states the bound for p-valent f(z) = z + sum b_n z^n. It says the conjecture 'has been verified for several special cases, including p-valent typically-real functions and certain classes of p-valent functions that generalize convex univalent functions'. It cites Wikipedia and a Project Euclid link, and says: 'This issue was generated by an AI agent and reviewed by me.' The issue has no human comments. It was closed as completed on 13 September 2026 via PR #4435.
events.revisions: Labels and milestone added 8 March 2026; closed 13 September 2026 by PR #4435.
events.delivers: Nothing mathematical. It is a formalisation request. Its special-case claim is asserted without a proof in the issue; the only sources it cites are Wikipedia and one Project Euclid link, which I did not open.
events.time_since_posted: about 6 months before closure (8 March to 13 September 2026)
events.doubts: The special-case claim is not tied to a specific reference in the issue body. The Wikipedia article I read names only p = 2 and 3 with P composed with phi, and does not mention typically-real functions. The typically-real claim comes from the Encyclopedia of Mathematics, which I could not open (502).
events.direction: Restates the conjecture and claims special cases; no direction of result.

events.what_happened: Pull request google-deepmind/formal-conjectures #4435, 'feat(Wikipedia): Goodman's conjecture on coefficients of p-valent functions', by GitHub user him1411, opened 14 July 2026, body 'Closes #3477', merged 13 September 2026 by mo271 through the merge queue (commit fc2696b). It adds FormalConjectures/Wikipedia/GoodmanConjecture.lean (+131 lines). The file defines IsPValent (analytic on the open unit ball; at most p distinct preimages of each value there, and exactly p for some value); coeff f n = iteratedDeriv n f 0 / n!; IsNormalized (map_zero : f 0 = 0 in the file I read); and goodmanBound f p n, the sum over k in 1..p of 2k(n+p)! / ((p-k)! (p+k)! (n-p-1)! (n^2 - k^2)) times the norm of coeff f k. The theorem goodman_conjecture takes p < n and states norm(coeff f n) <= goodmanBound f p n, with proof 'sorry', tagged research open, AMS 30. The one proved item is the test lemma goodmanBound_one, which reduces the p = 1 bound to n times |b_1|.
events.revisions: Review rounds 25 July to 13 September 2026; suggestion commits co-credited to Moritz Firsching applied before merge; merged 13 September 2026 as fc2696b.
events.delivers: A formal statement of the inequality for all p and n > p, with its proof left as sorry. It establishes no proof of the conjecture for any p or n. The only proved item is the p = 1 algebra lemma, which reduces the bound to n|b_1| and is not Bieberbach's theorem itself.
events.remains: All of problem_asks: the inequality for all p and all n > p.

events.doubts: (1) The PR description says IsNormalized fixes f(0) = 0 and f'(0) = 1. The raw file as I read it defines IsNormalized with only map_zero : f 0 = 0, and its docstring calls the normalisation f(0) = 0. The description and the file I read cannot both describe the merged version; I could not confirm which is merged. If the f'(0) = 1 normalisation is in force, the formal statement covers only b_1 = 1. (2) IsPValent counts distinct preimages in the open disk, not multiplicities. I reasoned that for interior points the two notions agree, but did not verify this. (3) The file takes n > p, so n = p+1 is included; the frozen bullet and the article give no range. None of this is a verdict on whether the formal statement matches the conjecture.
events.direction: The formal statement asserts the conjectured inequality; it neither supports nor cuts against it.

disputes.summary: Two secondary descriptions disagree on the scope of the 1951 Goodman-Robertson result: a restricted class T(p), against real coefficients for arbitrary p. Not resolved.

Wikipedia says the conjecture is known to hold for p = 2 and 3 when f = P composed with phi. The 1997 Grinshpan abstract describes a reduction for polynomial compositions, not a proof. Which source settles the p = 2, 3 cases is not identified in the text I read.

The 2026 issue asserts verified special cases (typically-real p-valent functions, and certain classes generalizing convex univalent functions). The Wikipedia article I read lists no such cases. Not reconciled.

summary: I found no mathematical progress on Goodman's coefficient inequality for p-valent functions since 26 January 2024. The partial results are all older and restricted: Goodman-Robertson 1951 (scope disputed between two secondary reports), Livingston 1969 (close-to-convex functions under a vanishing condition), Miniowitz 1976 (one case, possibly a different Goodman conjecture), Leach 1978 (real coefficients, a class including close-to-convex functions; abstract read), Todorov 1986 (p-th powers of univalent functions; abstract seen in a search result), and Grinshpan 1997 (polynomial compositions reduced to a several-variables conjecture; abstract read). Lyzzaik-Styer 1978 is cited for its determinant theorem but could not be read. The Wikipedia article I read says the conjecture is known for p = 2 and 3 when f is P composed with a univalent phi, and gives no general status. Every window source that addresses status treats the general conjecture as unproved: the Lean file is tagged research open, and the issue and the article list only special cases. The only window events are formal. Issue #3477 was opened 8 March 2026 and states verified special cases; its body says 'This issue was generated by an AI agent and reviewed by me'. PR #4435 was opened 14 July and merged 13 September 2026 (commit fc2696b). It adds a Lean statement of the inequality for all p and n > p, with the conjecture itself as sorry, and a proved p = 1 algebra lemma. Nothing in the window claims a proof, a counterexample or a bound. AI involvement: the only AI involvement found is the unnamed agent that generated the issue text. That is formalisation scaffolding, not mathematics, and no system is named. The PR shows no AI disclosure in the description or review comments I read. Searches: 35 web searches, plus fetches of the primary sources that were reachable. The AI search covered the OpenAI math catalogue (only 100 of 372 family names visible; no Goodman-related name), the AlphaProof Nexus results repository (top level only), the aimath tracker (most of its text read; no hit), kingy.ai (no Goodman record), and 2026 AI-math news (none mention this conjecture). The Manifold market (71% yes, no comments) is not evidence. The main gap is the citing literature for 2024 to 2026: the arXiv listing and zbMATH were blocked (403), and the arXiv API returned two unrelated entries. The 'nothing found' conclusion for the window therefore rests on web search, not on a bibliographic database. Close calls: whether the 2026 formal entry 'settles' anything (it does not; it is a statement with sorry), and whether the Lean IsNormalized includes f'(0) = 1 (the PR description says so; the file I read does not). Other 2024 to 2026 papers I saw are about other problems and are not events here: Qu 2024 (univalent theory and Bieberbach), Hamada, Kohr and Kohr 2024 (Bieberbach in Banach spaces), Krushkal 2026 (Zalcman and Bieberbach), and the kingy.ai Pommerenke record (2026, no AI role disclosed).
competing_reading: One can read the restricted results above (Todorov 1986, Leach 1978, Grinshpan 1997) and the Wikipedia 'known for p = 2, 3' sentence as a body of partial results, and the 2026 formal entry as a new formal record. Alternatively, the 1951 Goodman-Robertson paper can be read as covering real coefficients for every p, which would be a much larger partial result than the restricted-class reading. Against both: every source that addresses status calls the general conjecture unproved; the formal file carries sorry on the conjecture itself; and every partial result is restricted (p-th powers, real coefficients, close-to-convex functions, polynomial compositions). The larger reading matters only if the 1951 scope is confirmed.
what_would_settle_it: (a) Full texts of Goodman-Robertson 1951, Livingston 1969, Leach 1978 (full text), Todorov 1986, Lyzzaik-Styer 1978, and Miniowitz 1976; the AMS pages were blocked to the fetch tool, and a library copy would do. (b) The main-branch file and the merged commit fc2696b, to settle whether IsNormalized includes deriv f 0 = 1. (c) A zbMATH or MathSciNet citing search for Goodman's conjecture for 2024 to 2026, which was blocked here. (d) The full text of Hayman and Lingham 2018 (arXiv:1809.07200), to see how it lists the problem; its PDF was unreadable through the fetch tool. (e) The Wikipedia article's history, to find when the 'p = 2, 3' sentence was added and what it cites. (f) The rest of the OpenAI math CONTENTS.md and the rest of the aimath tracker.
